source.title: Intriguing Properties of Dynamic Sampling Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Ablation experiments on CIFAR-10 measure whether particular training configurations stabilize and train networks with dynamic sampling; this bears on training outcomes, though it does not test the claim's general random-initialization/near-zero-error recipe directly.
record.gate_note: Reported SelfWarp and deformable convolution training outcomes on CIFAR-10, plus a skip-connection accuracy comparison, are included. Cited results about other architectures are not rows. Stability thresholds define divergence; they are not separate outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses initialization variance analysis and residual architectures to analyze dynamic sampling. Its own results measure offset divergence and classification accuracy, without testing any version's specified training-error, depth, initialization-speed, learning-rate-threshold, or normalization-speed comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors identify two intrinsic sources of dynamic-sampling instability and argue that both require mitigation, supported by their ablations. They also conclude that spatial consistency improves accuracy and call for validation on larger models and datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains modified Resnet 56 and deformable convolution models with SelfWarp/warping and varies stabilization mechanisms; it does not test the claim's standard SGD/Adam random-initialization classification-error recipe. The authors describe the results as ablation studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Training stability and reported accuracy vary with pre-ε batch normalization, batch norm initialization, gradient handling/scaling, pretraining, and whether skip connections are warped.

fits_no_version.finding: Dynamic-sampling configurations differ in offset divergence and reported CIFAR-10 accuracy. Corrected Table 1 has five divergent configurations and three accuracies: 92.378%, 93.620%, and 93.209%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stable training of the tested dynamic-sampling networks requires jointly controlling forward-variance dependence and excess gradients through the offset branch.

fits_no_version.finding: Warping skip connections yields 93.620% accuracy versus 92.919% when those connections remain unwarped.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintaining spatial consistency by warping skip connections improves reported CIFAR-10 accuracy in the tested SelfWarp ResNet-56.

record.problems: The reported table outcomes are accuracy or divergence, not training classification error. The text does not report trial counts, uncertainty, or a capability check. The experiments use a Resnet 56 model on CIFAR-10 and do not vary depth, width, or dataset for the central ablations.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying study results omitted. The paper's figure-only training dynamics and loss landscapes do not report a claim-version outcome; the referenced Resnet accuracy comparison and Table 1 and Table 2 entries are included.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and effects of size, early stopping, or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and benefits of extra student neurons.
Training error across depths with and without identity shortcuts; deep plain tanh networks and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and deep orthogonal convolutions.
Learning rates relative to initial stability thresholds, transient loss growth and recovery, and sharpness trajectories.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy gain over training time and learning-rate tolerance; normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 values are misaligned in the record from R4 onward. Divergence denotes an offset-variance threshold crossing at any point; the authors explicitly allow subsequent recovery. It therefore does not by itself establish persistent failure to reach low training error. Accuracy split and statistical uncertainty are not specified in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach near-zero training classification error, including on CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks as a function of depth and training error, and training of deep plain tanh networks or normalization-free residual networks.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for signal propagation, speed, and trainable depth in plain networks.
Training above learning-rate stability limits and sharpness behavior.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or increases learning-rate tolerance in the named architectures; Fixup comparisons.
